lines.en: Lina, did you see that woman? She walked straight into a lamp post. She must have been using her phone.
lines.pt: Lina, você viu aquela mulher? Ela bateu direto num poste. Ela devia estar usando o celular.

lines.en: Probably! She was staring at her hands the whole time, so she was totally oblivious to the pedestrians around her.
lines.pt: Provavelmente! Ela olhou para as mãos o tempo todo, então estava totalmente alheia aos pedestres ao redor.

lines.en: Or maybe she was listening to music. I saw white headphones, but she wasn't looking where she was going either way.
lines.pt: Ou talvez estivesse ouvindo música. Vi fones brancos, mas ela não olhava por onde andava de qualquer jeito.

lines.en: Poor thing. She looked so embarrassed when everyone turned around. She must have been feeling terrible, because she hurried off without looking at anyone.
lines.pt: Coitada. Ela ficou tão constrangida quando todos se viraram. Devia estar se sentindo péssima, porque saiu apressada sem olhar para ninguém.

lines.en: She can't have been hurt, though. She laughed and kept walking. Maybe she was laughing at herself, which is the best way to react.
lines.pt: Mas ela não pode ter se machucado. Riu e continuou andando. Talvez estivesse rindo de si mesma, que é a melhor maneira de reagir.

lines.en: True. Remember when I tripped over a curb in front of the whole class? I must have been reading a message, and I'd noticed nothing.
lines.pt: Verdade. Lembra quando tropecei na calçada na frente da turma toda? Devia estar lendo uma mensagem, e não tinha reparado em nada.

lines.en: Ha, I remember! You went bright red, and then you pretended you'd dropped something. You were so convincing.
lines.pt: Ha, eu lembro! Você ficou vermelha como um tomate e fingiu que tinha derrubado alguma coisa. Foi muito convincente.

lines.en: Look at that guy across the street, the one walking so fast. He's late for something, or he's running from a bad date.
lines.pt: Olha aquele cara do outro lado da rua, o que anda tão rápido. Ele está atrasado para algo, ou fugindo de um encontro ruim.

lines.en: He might have been rushing to catch the metro. These boulevards get crazy at six o'clock, and everybody just pushes through.
lines.pt: Talvez estivesse correndo para pegar o metrô. Esses bulevares ficam malucos às seis da tarde, e todo mundo vai se empurrando pelo caminho.

lines.en: I love watching them, though. It reminds me of that painting, Boulevard Montmartre at Night, with all the lights and the tiny people.
lines.pt: Eu adoro observá-los, no entanto. Isso me lembra aquele quadro, Boulevard Montmartre à noite, com todas as luzes e as pessoas minúsculas.

lines.en: Same! Let's grab a table at that café and keep people-watching until the lights come on.
lines.pt: Também! Vamos pegar uma mesa naquele café e continuar observando as pessoas até as luzes acenderem.

facts.label: Dedução sobre o passado
facts.sub: Quase certeza sobre ação em andamento: She must have been texting. Negativa: can not have been. Menos certeza: might have been.

facts.label: Must have been
facts.sub: Para deduzir uma ação em andamento no passado: She must have been using her phone. Você tem quase certeza, mas não viu. Estrutura: must + have + been + verbo-ing.

facts.label: Can not have been
facts.sub: Para negar uma dedução, use can not ou could not: She can not have been sleeping. Evite mustn’t have been, que soa pouco natural em inglês britânico e americano.

pages.title: The lamp post accident · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a sunny afternoon on a busy street in Adelaide. Eli and Zoe are waiting for a bus. Crowds of people pass by. Most of them stare at their phones. Suddenly there is a loud bang. A woman has hit a lamp post.

“Zoe, did you see that woman? She walked straight into a lamp post. She must have been using her phone.” says Eli. “Probably. She must have been reading a message, because she was staring at her hands the whole time.” says Zoe. “Or she must have been listening to music. She was wearing headphones, so she was oblivious to everything.” says Eli.
